title: Primitive Subspaces Mediate Few-Shot Transfer in VLAs
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens (OpenVLA) and flow/diffusion action expert (pi0.5, 16-step chunks as described)
methods: 2x2 training design (flat vs primitive-segmented data) x 2 architectures x 3 seeds
demo-conditioned few-shot transfer by prepending mean-pooled vision features of m demos to the prompt
linear probes for primitive identity at layers 8/16/24/final
4-dim probe-subspace ablation (orthogonal projection, Ravfogel/Belrose style) vs random-subspace control
question: Does training VLAs on primitive-segmented episodes create a primitive subspace that is causally necessary for few-shot composition of held-out tasks?
key_findings: REASSEMBLE, 6 held-out tasks, m = 3 demos: primitive-trained 0.62 +/- 0.04 (OpenVLA) and 0.66 +/- 0.04 (pi0.5) vs flat 0.34 +/- 0.06 and 0.31 +/- 0.05; at m = 10 flat reaches 0.61 / 0.58; fine-tuned upper bound (50 demos) 0.79 / 0.82 (Table 2).
LIBERO-Long replication at m = 3: primitive 0.71 / 0.74 vs flat 0.42 / 0.45 (ratio 1.66x).
Out-of-vocabulary primitive (rotate-to-engage): primitive training hurts, 0.08 +/- 0.03 vs flat 0.14 +/- 0.04 at m = 5 (OpenVLA).
Probe macro-F1 for primitive identity (layers 16-24): 0.79-0.81 primitive-trained vs 0.48-0.52 flat-trained; decodability correlates with few-shot success at r = 0.73.

Ablating the 4-dim probe subspace at layer 24: 0.62 -> 0.30 (OpenVLA) and 0.66 -> 0.34 (pi0.5); a random 4-dim subspace: 0.62 -> 0.60 and 0.66 -> 0.64 (Table 4, 10 random samples). On training-distribution tasks the same ablation only drops 0.84 -> 0.79.
Octo-style demo-conditioned baseline 0.41 (OpenVLA comparison) / 0.44 vs primitive few-shot 0.62 / 0.66 at m = 3.
Single-step 3-sigma action gates applied element-wise fail 42% of ground-truth pi0.5-format 16-step chunks vs 2.0% for OpenVLA format, a family-wise inflation artifact.

evidence.setting: simulation (as stated by the authors; the REASSEMBLE rollout environment is not described)
benchmarks: REASSEMBLE (NIST Task Board 1), 6 held-out object-task combinations plus an out-of-vocabulary task
evidence.scale: 50 rollouts per cell, 3 training seeds per cell; probes trained on 2,000 held-out demos
evidence.statistics: partial: mean +/- SD across 3 seeds and 95% bootstrap CIs mentioned; no formal tests for the main contrasts
evidence.baselines: flat-trained few-shot, zero-shot primitive sequencing with external planner (0.04 alone), Octo-Small demo-conditioned, CNN Diffusion Policy, 50-demo LoRA fine-tuning upper bound

causal_validation: Claimed yes: probe-subspace ablation with a random-subspace control and a specificity check on in-distribution tasks. However, the paper's own figure captions describe the numbers as 'illustrative pending verification', so the causal evidence cannot be taken at face value.
closed_loop: Reported as closed-loop success rates, but the environment for REASSEMBLE rollouts is never specified.
limitations_stated: Three seeds give wide per-cell variance (SD 0.03-0.06).
External task-to-primitive planner because openpi does not expose text generation.
Ablation shows necessity of the subspace, not that primitive supervision is the only way to create it.
critique: Credibility red flag: the captions of Figure 2 and Figure 3 (main results and the causal ablation) say 'Numbers are illustrative pending verification'. Until a verified version exists, these results should not be cited as evidence.
The paper never names a simulator for REASSEMBLE, yet reports 50 rollouts per cell with millimetre-level success criteria; how REASSEMBLE tasks were executed is unclear.

A 'layer-24' probe and ablation is reported for both models, but other papers in this batch describe pi0/pi0.5's PaliGemma backbone as having 18 layers (2509.00328, 2511.22697), so the pi0.5 intervention site is unclear.
How mean-pooled vision features are 'prepended to the language prompt' of models never trained to accept them is not explained; few-shot gains without any training of this pathway are surprising.
Results are unusually clean and symmetric across architectures, datasets and seeds; with no released code ('upon publication') and no funding disclosure, treat as unverified.
If verified, the design (random-subspace control, in-distribution specificity check, negative OOV result) would be among the better causal designs in the batch.
one_line: Claims that training OpenVLA and pi0.5 on primitive-segmented data creates a linearly decodable primitive subspace that is causally needed for few-shot composition of new assembly tasks, but the paper labels its own key figures as illustrative and unverified.
